investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-17T00:54–01:02Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a schedulable state, so the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource quota on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for peer-pod VMs at the time of the eval run. Because the pod never started, the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (lines 1880–1885) could not reach createAgent() completion, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the contract validation to fail entirely (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence).

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready'] — neither assertion can be evaluated without a running pod.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource slots on the 2 eligible nodes are fully consumed by existing running remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new pods at the time of the eval run.

[Likely] The 4 remaining nodes lack the required node affinity label or taint toleration for remote-agent pods (e.g., a node selector or affinity rule targeting kata/peerpods nodes), so they are structurally ineligible regardless of resource availability.
[Possible] A prior eval run or user-initiated remote agent was not cleaned up and is holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, preventing new scheduling.
[Possible] The cluster was recently scaled down or nodes were cordoned/drained, reducing the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously larger pool to only 2.
[Lower likelihood] A quota or LimitRange applied at the namespace level is capping the number of peer-pod VMs allowed concurrently, and that cap has been reached.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-17T00:54–01:02Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a schedulable state, so the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource quota on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for peer-pod VMs at the time of the eval run. Because the pod never started, the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (lines 1880–1885) could not reach createAgent() completion, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the contract validation to fail entirely (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence).

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource slots on the 2 eligible nodes are fully consumed by existing running remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new pods at the time of the eval run.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Kubernetes Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Blocks All Remote Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every eval attempt to provision a remote agent pod was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Unschedulable: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm". The pod never started, so no agent evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was ever produced, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. Of the 6 total nodes, 4 do not match the pod's node affinity/selector and are therefore ineligible, leaving only 2 schedulable nodes — both of which report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm". Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted by the eval runner remains in Pending/Unschedulable state until the probe timeout fires, and no agent runtime response is ever returned. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool in the production-api environment; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — no capacity remains for new remote agent pods, and preemption found no victims to evict. All three sibling checks report the identical scheduler message, confirming this is a shared infrastructure constraint, not an isolated probe issue.

[Secondary] Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift — 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, artificially shrinking the schedulable pool to 2 nodes. If affinity rules were recently tightened or node labels changed, the effective capacity would drop even if total cluster size is unchanged.

[Less likely] A long-running or leaked remote agent pod from a prior eval run is holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and was not cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper visible at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1916. This would reduce available VM slots without increasing cluster capacity.

[Speculative] The cluster was scaled down or nodes were cordoned/drained, reducing the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously higher count to the current 2, without a corresponding reduction in concurrent pod demand.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 affinity-matching nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity still available (i.e., not exhausted), the root cause is not pool exhaustion and another scheduler constraint must be investigated.

If re-running the eval immediately after this failure produces a passing result with all 5 evidence fields present, the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a prior eval pod was still terminating) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are shown to have kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the affinity rules are confirmed to be intentionally restrictive, the root cause shifts to node affinity misconfiguration rather than pool exhaustion.
If no pods from prior eval runs are found holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, the leak hypothesis is disproved and the cause is either true capacity exhaustion or a cluster scaling event.

If local-agent checks (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) pass in the same run window, that would confirm the failure is isolated to the remote VM pool and not a broader agent infrastructure or API outage.
